title: 2023 parking strategy and downtown patio concerns
subtitle: Pierpoint heritage landscape, speed limit reductions, Beatty Line reconstruction, business park servicing, vehicle purchases and fee amendments.
overview: Council approved the 2023 parking strategy {{vote:m3}}. It continues third-party parking enforcement, a Fergus to Elora shuttle with a new stop, and the Provost Lane closure in Fergus. There will be no planned street closures in Elora while East Mill Street is under construction. Several downtown Elora residents and business owners raised concerns about extended patios, lost parking, safety and noise, while a patio operator spoke in support. Staff said a longer-term parking strategy is planned for 2024.

Council also moved to protect Pierpoint history. It added the Pierpoint Fly Fishing Nature Reserve to the cultural heritage landscape inventory and directed staff to pursue heritage designation {{vote:m2}}. It endorsed lower speed limits on some roads and doubled the 2023 traffic calming budget {{vote:m4}}.

Council awarded the Beatty Line reconstruction contract {{vote:m5}} and the Business Park Phase 2 servicing contract {{vote:m6}}. It also approved vehicle purchases {{vote:m7}} and fee amendments {{vote:m8}}. Council heard a community improvement plan update and a request for a pocket disc golf course. Neither required a decision.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2023 strategy and authorized agreements for parking enforcement, a parking lot at 739 St Andrew St W for shuttle use, and bus and taxi shuttle services.

Council received the research report, added the Pierpoint Fly Fishing Nature Reserve as a significant cultural heritage landscape, and directed staff to report on Ontario Heritage Act designation and a community working group.

decisions.item: Speed limit reductions and traffic calming
decisions.detail: Council endorsed proposed speed limit reductions, directed staff to implement speed reduction measures, and raised the traffic calming budget from $125,000 to $250,000.
Council awarded the tender to Cox Construction Limited at $4,606,609.10 including contingency and excluding HST, and updated project funding.
Council awarded the servicing contract to Ersman Construction Inc. at $2,109,862.49 including contingency and excluding HST.
Council authorized buying two SUVs, five half-ton pickups and one electric vehicle from named suppliers and revised the related funding.
Council endorsed amendments to the 2023 Fees & Charges By-law for planning and development fees, road occupancy permits and housekeeping items.
Council nominated John Sepulis as municipal representative for Municipal Grouping Number 1 on the Lake Erie Source Protection Committee.

debate: Delegates from downtown Elora said extended patios take parking and sidewalk space and create safety risks for pedestrians. They also raised noise and over-serving, asked for equal treatment of all businesses, and said patios should be a privilege that can be withheld.

A patio operator's representative said patios were built at the Township's urging, cost significant sums and bring in jobs and revenue. The operators carry liability insurance and are willing to work with regulators.

Staff said the patio by-law does not make liquor licensing or complaint history a permit criterion, and that alcohol licensing is a provincial matter. Staff cautioned against reopening the by-law and said complaints would be tracked. Councillors asked about accessible parking, resident parking permits and shuttle ridership, which staff said was poor last year.

A rural delegate supported a four-way stop at Second Line and Sideroad 20. The delegate opposed lowering the Second Line speed limit, citing a lack of enforcement, observations taken during bridge-closure traffic, and no stated expected outcomes. Staff said follow-up monitoring is part of the process and offered to notify residents and review another intersection.
On the community improvement plan, councillors encouraged broader support for rural and agricultural uses and a higher unit cap for rental housing grants. The consultant said both could be changed.
